points.title: 贵族童年
points.description: 纳博科夫出生于圣彼得堡一个显赫的自由派贵族家庭。他的父亲弗拉基米尔·德米特里耶维奇·纳博科夫是著名的宪法律师和政治家，母亲是富有的犹太裔工业家的女儿。这个家庭拥有巨大的财富和广泛的文化联系，为纳博科夫提供了优越的教育环境。他从小接受多语言教育，精通俄语、英语和法语，后来又学习了拉丁语、希腊语和德语。这段时期，他阅读了大量文学作品，特别是俄罗斯和欧洲的经典著作，培养了敏锐的审美意识和语言天赋。
points.descriptionEn: Nabokov was born in Saint Petersburg into a prominent aristocratic family. His father, Dmitry Nabokov, was a prominent liberal statesman and lawyer, while his mother came from a wealthy Jewish industrialist family. This privileged upbringing provided Nabokov with exceptional education and cultural exposure. He was multilingual from childhood, mastering Russian, English, French, and later Latin, Greek, and German. During this period, he immersed himself in literature, particularly Russian and European classics, developing his sophisticated literary taste and linguistic abilities that would later define his writing style.

points.title: 剑桥求学
points.description: 1919年，纳博科夫随家人流亡到英国，进入剑桥大学三一学院学习动物学、斯拉夫语和罗曼语系。在剑桥期间，他开始创作诗歌和短篇小说，并加入了剑桥使徒社这个精英知识分子团体。1920年，他发表了第一部诗集《诗集》。这段时期，他形成了自己独特的文学观，强调艺术形式和语言美感的重要性，同时开始对蝴蝶学产生浓厚兴趣，这一爱好贯穿了他的一生。1922年，他从剑桥毕业，继续在欧洲大陆游历。
points.descriptionEn: In 1919, following the Russian Revolution, Nabokov went into exile and enrolled at Trinity College, Cambridge, where he studied zoology, Slavic languages, and Romance languages. During his Cambridge years, he began writing poetry and short stories, and joined the Cambridge Apostles, an intellectual society. In 1920, he published his first collection of poetry, 'Poems.' This period was crucial in forming his literary philosophy, emphasizing artistic form and linguistic beauty. He also developed a lifelong passion for lepidopterology (butterfly studies), which would become a significant part of his life and work.

points.title: 流亡作家
points.description: 1922年，纳博科夫移居柏林，开始了长达十八年的流亡生活。他在柏林大学教授俄语文学，同时以笔名V. Sirin创作了大量作品。1925年，他与犹太裔妻子薇拉结婚。这一时期，他创作了《玛丽》、《王后棋》、《暗中的火》等重要作品，确立了作为俄语作家的声誉。1937年，纳博科夫因纳粹上台而离开德国，先移居法国巴黎，1940年移居美国。柏林时期是纳博科夫创作的第一个高峰，他发展了自己独特的叙事技巧和对细节的执着追求，这些特点后来成为他作品的标志。
points.descriptionEn: In 1922, Nabokov moved to Berlin, beginning eighteen years of exile. He taught Russian literature in Berlin and wrote under the pseudonym V. Sirin. In 1925, he married his Jewish wife, Véra Slonim. During this period, he wrote major works including 'Mary,' 'The King, Queen, Jack,' and 'The Eye,' establishing his reputation as a Russian writer. In 1937, following the rise of Nazism, Nabokov left Germany, first moving to Paris, then to the United States in 1940. His Berlin years marked his first creative peak, where he developed his distinctive narrative techniques and obsession with detail that would become hallmarks of his work.

points.title: 美国学者
points.description: 1940年，纳博科夫移居美国，开始在韦尔斯利学院教授俄罗斯文学，后又在康奈尔大学任教。这一时期，他开始用英语创作，1955年出版了最具争议也最著名的作品《洛丽塔》。《洛丽塔》的出版引发了巨大争议，被多国列为禁书，但也确立了纳博科夫作为英语世界重要作家的地位。同时，他继续从事蝴蝶学研究，在大都会自然博物馆工作，并发现了多种蝴蝶新品种。纳博科夫的美国经历丰富了他的创作视野，他将欧洲文化背景与美国社会观察相结合，形成了独特的跨文化视角。
points.descriptionEn: In 1940, Nabokov moved to the United States, teaching Russian literature at Wellesley College and later at Cornell University. During this period, he began writing in English, publishing his most controversial and famous work, 'Lolita,' in 1955. 'Lolita' sparked immense controversy and was banned in several countries, but it established Nabokov as a major figure in English literature. He also continued his lepidopterology research, working at the American Museum of Natural History and discovering several new butterfly species. His American experience broadened his creative perspective, combining European cultural background with American social observations to form a unique cross-cultural viewpoint.

points.title: 欧洲回归
points.description: 1959年，纳博科夫移居瑞士蒙特勒，度过了他生命的最后十八年。在瑞士期间，他继续创作并翻译自己的作品，包括将《洛丽塔》翻译成俄语。1962年，他出版了《微暗的火》，这部实验性小说被许多评论家认为是他的杰作。1964年，他完成了自传《说吧，记忆》，详细记录了他的早年生活和流亡经历。纳博科夫在瑞士过着相对隐居的生活，专注于写作和研究蝴蝶学，直到1977年去世。瑞士时期是纳博科夫创作的又一个高峰，他的作品更加成熟和复杂，对语言和形式的探索达到了新的高度。
points.descriptionEn: In 1959, Nabokov moved to Montreux, Switzerland, where he spent the last eighteen years of his life. During this Swiss period, he continued writing and translating his works, including translating 'Lolita' into Russian. In 1962, he published 'Pale Fire,' an experimental novel many critics consider his masterpiece. In 1964, he completed his autobiography 'Speak, Memory,' detailing his early life and exile experiences. Nabokov lived a relatively reclusive life in Switzerland, focusing on writing and lepidopterology until his death in 1977. His Swiss years represented another creative peak, with his works becoming more mature and complex, reaching new heights in his exploration of language and form.

points.title: 文学遗产
points.description: 1977年7月2日，纳博科夫在瑞士克莱朗去世，享年78岁。他的葬礼在附近的洛桑举行，遗体火化后安葬在瑞士。纳博科夫去世后，他的文学地位得到进一步巩固，被公认为20世纪最重要的作家之一。他的作品被翻译成多种语言，影响了几代作家。他的独特写作风格、对语言的精确掌控、复杂的叙事结构以及对细节的执着追求，成为后世作家学习和模仿的对象。同时，他的蝴蝶学研究也获得了学术界的认可，他发现的蝴蝶品种以他的名字命名。纳博科夫的遗产超越了文学领域，成为跨文化创作和艺术追求的典范。
points.descriptionEn: On July 2, 1977, Nabokov died in Clarens, Switzerland, at the age of 78. His funeral was held in nearby Lausanne, and his remains were cremated and buried in Switzerland. After his death, Nabokov's literary status was further solidified, and he is widely regarded as one of the most important writers of the 20th century. His works have been translated into numerous languages and have influenced generations of writers. His distinctive writing style, precise command of language, complex narrative structures, and obsession with detail have become objects of study and emulation for later writers. Simultaneously, his lepidopterology research gained academic recognition, with butterfly species named after him. Nabokov's legacy extends beyond literature, becoming a model for cross-cultural creation and artistic pursuit.

appraisal.zh: 纳博科夫通常被看作语言大师和现代主义文学的重要创新者，以精确的语言、复杂的结构和丰富的想象力打破传统叙事，对细节与美的执着使平凡场景化为艺术体验，《洛丽塔》虽引发争议，仍被许多人视为20世纪最重要的小说之一，其跨文化背景也赋予他独特视角。另一种看法认为，他过分注重形式而缺乏深度，精英姿态与对社会政治的冷漠使他疏离时代，作品缺少道德关怀，《洛丽塔》被指美化恋童，晦涩风格也远离普通读者，对个人记忆的依赖限制了其广度。
appraisal.en: Nabokov is generally seen as a master of language and a major modernist innovator, breaking with traditional narrative through precise prose, complex structure and rich imagination; his devotion to detail and beauty turns ordinary scenes into artistic experience, and Lolita, though controversial, is widely counted among the most important novels of the twentieth century, his cross-cultural background lending him a distinctive perspective. Another view holds that he prized form over depth, that his elitist stance and indifference to social and political life detached him from his era, that his work lacks moral concern and that Lolita romanticizes pedophilia, while his obscure style alienates ordinary readers and his reliance on personal memory limits his range.

supporter.zh: 纳博科夫被支持者视为语言大师和文学创新者，他的作品以其精确的语言、复杂的结构和丰富的想象力著称。他打破了传统叙事的界限，创造了独特的文学世界。纳博科夫对细节的执着追求和对美的敏感使他能够将普通场景转化为艺术体验。他的《洛丽塔》虽然引发争议，但被许多人认为是20世纪最重要的小说之一，展示了作者对语言的掌控能力和对人性的深刻洞察。纳博科夫的跨文化背景使他能够以独特的视角审视世界，他的作品超越了文化和语言的界限，成为普遍人性的探索。
supporter.en: Supporters view Nabokov as a master of language and literary innovation, whose works are celebrated for their precise language, complex structures, and rich imagination. He broke the boundaries of traditional narrative, creating unique literary worlds. Nabokov's obsession with detail and sensitivity to beauty allowed him to transform ordinary scenes into artistic experiences. Though controversial, 'Lolita' is considered by many as one of the most important novels of the 20th century, demonstrating the author's command of language and profound insight into human nature. His cross-cultural background enabled him to examine the world from a unique perspective, and his works transcend cultural and linguistic boundaries to explore universal humanity.

critic.zh: 批评者认为纳博科夫的作品过于注重形式而缺乏深度，他的精英主义态度和对社会政治的冷漠使他脱离了时代。一些评论家指责他的作品缺乏道德关怀，特别是《洛丽塔》被批评为美化恋童癖。他的复杂叙事和晦涩风格也被认为是故作高深，远离普通读者。此外，纳博科夫对俄罗斯流亡经历的浪漫化处理和对苏联的敌视态度也受到质疑。批评者认为他过于依赖个人记忆和主观体验，而忽视了更广阔的社会和历史背景，这限制了他作品的深度和广度。
critic.en: Critics argue that Nabokov's works过分注重形式而缺乏深度，他的 elitist attitude and indifference to social and political issues detached him from his时代. Some commentators accuse his works of lacking moral concern, particularly 'Lolita,' which was criticized for romanticizing pedophilia. His complex narratives and obscure style were also seen as pretentious and inaccessible to ordinary readers. Additionally, Nabokov's romanticized portrayal of his exile experience and his anti-Soviet stance were questioned. Critics contend that his over-reliance on personal memory and subjective experience, while neglecting broader social and historical contexts, limited the depth and breadth of his work.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，纳博科夫被定义为一位重要的现代主义作家和语言大师，他的作品体现了20世纪文学实验的精髓。他的跨文化身份使他成为全球化文学的先驱，影响了后殖民文学的发展。纳博科夫的蝴蝶学研究也获得了学术认可，展示了他在科学领域的贡献。在流行文化中，他的名字与《洛丽塔》紧密相连，这部作品已成为文化符号，被多次改编为电影和戏剧。纳博科夫的写作风格影响了包括萨尔曼·拉什迪、马丁·艾米斯在内的众多作家，他的文学遗产持续影响着当代文学创作和文学理论的发展。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Nabokov is defined as an important modernist writer and master of language, whose works embody the essence of 20th-century literary experimentation. His cross-cultural identity makes him a pioneer of globalized literature, influencing the development of postcolonial literature. Nabokov's lepidopterology research has also gained academic recognition, demonstrating his contributions to science. In popular culture, his name is inextricably linked with 'Lolita,' which has become a cultural symbol, adapted into films and plays multiple times. Nabokov's writing style has influenced numerous writers including Salman Rushdie and Martin Amis, and his literary legacy continues to shape contemporary literary creation and theory.

self.zh: 文学是细节的艺术，而细节是记忆的结晶。
self.en: Literature is the art of discovery, and the discovery of the detail.
